section.title: Holding the Bubble
section.form_description: A speech meant to move someone to act — the narrator talking Shepard (or whoever is listening) up off the floor and back into the fight. Sections are the rising beats of an address: the stakes named, the doubt named plainly, the evidence from a life lived that it can be done, the call. The narrator's own history is fuel for the exhortation, not the subject of it — but so is the listener's: the narrator holds up the other person's record as often as their own, since it's their record the speech is meant to land on.
section.form_note:
The brief is a speech, not a life story: Jack talking Shepard up in the last hour before the last push, using her own record as proof it can be done. Set after the Cerberus coup, the Citadel DLC shore leave, and the Cronos Station assault, this is the morning of the London conduit assault on Earth — everything is already staged (ships loaded, the plan set, the crew briefed), and the only thing left to do is get up and launch it. Jack is rousing Shepard right before he walks out to fight, not settling him in for the night. Romanced Jack per canon.choices (romance: Jack), consummated per jack_meeting/normandy-engineering scene at the end of ME2, with the Citadel DLC back tattoo. Note: choices.yaml's citadel_coup detail says Thane "died protecting the dalatrass," but the event record (thane-krios-death-defending-the-salarian-councilor) and the coup scene (citadel-coup-csec-office-kai-leng) both have him dying for the Salarian Councilor — treating this as the user's shorthand slip, not a real contradiction, and writing it as the Councilor. Per Thomas's request, "what-cerberus-made-me-for" and "the-kids-at-grissom" were rebuilt off shared Shepard/Jack history and broader lore instead of the Teltin and Grissom backstory events: recruitment off the Purgatory prison ship (jack-recruitment-purgatory) plus the Jack/Miranda confrontation Shepard settled (jack_miranda_dispute: appeased both), and the Suicide Mission itself (Jack held the biotic barrier, all-survived outcome per suicide_mission canon). Pragia/Teltin and Grissom get at most a glancing bridging mention, never the anchor. Jack's framing of "holding a barrier is a focus problem, not a strength problem" and "Cerberus bought a weapon and Shepard made a person" are her own editorializing on the record, not new corpus facts.
Revision per Thomas: Shepard's own AU record is now a load-bearing second thread, not a token mention. Jack is pitching HIM back to himself — every section now carries at least one beat where she cites something true of Shepard specifically as the proof, not just her own Purgatory/barrier/Brimstone/Murtock record. Sourced from config/canon/choices.yaml's Shepard AU overrides (Normandy-born, no parents, gang and drug problem before Anderson pulled him into N7; Sole Survivor of Akuze, the whole squad dead but him; Vanguard, biotic charge into the guns; alignment "Paragon, except against oppressors"; first name Thomas) plus the ME2/ME3 record most relevant to a focus-and-resolve pitch: Cerberus rebuilding him from a corpse via the Lazarus Project (a direct mirror to Jack's own tank), Mordin's death at the Shroud finishing the genophage cure, and Thessia — the one fight where Kai Leng actually got the better of him and walked off with Vendetta, which Jack uses as the counter-example, not the insult. Kai Leng's death at Cronos Station, days earlier in the same push on Cerberus's headquarters, closes the speech as proof the focus she's asking for is already proven, not a new trick.
Second revision per Thomas, correcting two errors: (1) the outline had previously let the closing section cite the Illusive Man's suicide as settled proof Jack could point back to. That confrontation happens on the Citadel, concurrent with or immediately after the London conduit assault itself — part of the endgame this speech is walking Shepard out the door toward, not something resolved before it. It has been cut entirely; Kai Leng's death at Cronos Station (a distinct, already-resolved event from the assault on Cerberus's headquarters, which happened before this morning) carries that closing beat on its own. (2) the whole episode was misdated as the evening before, ending in the two of them going to sleep. It is corrected throughout to the morning of the assault itself: the fleet is already massed, the plan already briefed, nothing left to prepare — Jack is waking Shepard and getting him moving, not tucking him in. No section still ends on rest; every "tonight"/"tomorrow" reference has been changed to "today," "now," or "in the next hour," and "The Last Quiet Night" is renamed "The Last Quiet Hour" to hold the tattoo-and-sentiment beat inside a tense pre-launch hush instead of an evening of repose. The Crucible's final choice and Shepard's fate at the end of it remain deliberately left out: that hasn't happened yet either, and reaching for it would still be narrator omniscience, not something Jack could actually voice this morning.
This does not strain the form. `motivational`'s brief is explicit that "the narrator's own history is fuel for the exhortation, not the subject of it" — and Jack's whole method here is to make Shepard's history do exactly that work on Shepard himself: he's not telling her own story for its own sake, she's holding up his record as the evidence because a room full of only Jack's proof lets him nod along without it landing on him. Spine stays `mixed` — some sections anchor to Jack's own events/scenes, some to Shepard's, most to both at once, which is precisely what a speech that argues from the listener's own life looks like structurally. No change to form.

required_facts.fact: After acquiring a Reaper IFF and repelling a Collector boarding action that carried off the Normandy's non-combat crew, Commander Shepard took the Normandy SR-2 through the Omega 4 Relay to the Collector Base, a station on the accretion disk of a black hole in the galactic core. The ship survived the Collectors' Oculi and security systems, destroyed an intercepting Collector Cruiser, and crash-landed on the base. The assault ran in three segments. In "Infiltration," Shepard sent a tech specialist (ideally a loyal Legion, Tali, or Kasumi) through a thermal vent while a second fire-team leader (ideally Garrus, Miranda, or Jacob) ran a diversion; a non-ideal or non-loyal choice for either role got the vent specialist killed. In "The Long Walk," the squad reached the pods holding the abducted crew and colonists: whoever occupied the first opened pod was liquefied (Lilith of Horizon if Shepard rushed the mission, Yeoman Kelly Chambers if Shepard had delayed). The whole crew, half, or only Dr. Chakwas survived depending on how many missions Shepard ran after the abduction (`iff_delay`); assigning a squadmate to escort the survivors back to the ship saved the crew but pulled that squadmate from the finale, while sending no escort doomed the crew. The squad then advanced under a biotic barrier held by a biotic specialist (ideally a loyal Samara, Jack, or Morinth); a weak choice meant the rear-guard squadmate was carried off by Seeker Swarms in a fixed death order. A non-ideal second fire-team leader was shot dead on reaching the door. In "Final Battle," Shepard picked a squad and left the rest to hold the line; if that holding force's collective defense value was too low, members died in a fixed order starting with the non-loyal (Mordin first if present). Shepard destroyed the four feeding tubes of a Human-Reaper larva built from thousands of liquefied humans, dropping it into the chasm. The Illusive Man then asked Shepard to preserve the base with a radiation pulse instead of destroying it (`collector_base`): destroying it is the Paragon option, preserving it Renegade. The reactivated Human-Reaper was destroyed a second time, and the Normandy outran the base's end. If Shepard alone survived, Joker failed to pull the Commander aboard and Shepard fell to their death. Afterward Joker handed Shepard Reaper schematics as a fleet of Reapers was shown advancing on the Milky Way.
The Collector threat to human colonies ended; the Collectors were effectively wiped out as a force.
A Human-Reaper larva under construction from abducted humans was destroyed.

Per `iff_delay` / `kelly_chambers`: the abducted Normandy crew were rescued whole, partially (only some, including Chakwas), or reduced to Dr. Chakwas alone, based on how long Shepard delayed after installing the Reaper IFF; the first pod victim (Lilith or Kelly Chambers) was always liquefied.

Per `suicide_mission` / `loyalty_missions`: any combination of squadmates could die — the vent tech, the biotic specialist, either fire-team leader, the crew escort, the members left to hold the line, and finally Shepard — determined by loyalty status and role assignments; with all squad loyal and ideal assignments, everyone survives.
If only Shepard survived the mission, Shepard died falling back to the Normandy and the Illusive Man was met by Joker instead.

Per `collector_base`: the base was destroyed (radiation-and-explosion, Paragon) or preserved intact via a radiation pulse handed to Cerberus (Renegade). Destroying it left the Illusive Man furious; preserving it left him pleased.

In Mass Effect 3 the choice yields a War Asset from the salvaged Human-Reaper: a Reaper Brain (Military Strength 110, favors Control) if preserved, or a Reaper Heart (Military Strength 100, favors Destroy) if destroyed; Cerberus built the remains into Cronos Station regardless.
Surviving squadmates return or become War Assets in Mass Effect 3; the death of Legion or Tali makes a peaceful end to the geth-quarian war impossible.
Shepard obtained a datapad of Reaper schematics, and the imminent Reaper invasion of the Milky Way was revealed.

scenes.title: Suicide Mission Briefing Before Collector Base Infiltration
scenes.when: 2185, after crash-landing on the Collector Base, before the assault begins

beats.text: Shepard and the crew gather in the Normandy's briefing room as EDI projects a scan of the Collector Base's layout. EDI identifies the station's weak point in the central control center—likely where the captured Normandy crew and remaining colonists are held. Two routes lead to the center, but both require a tech specialist to pass through a thermal vent and open the way for two squads. Shepard selects the specialist: ideally a loyal Legion, Tali, or Kasumi, though any of these can be chosen regardless of loyalty at greater risk—a non-ideal choice will result in the specialist being shot before closing the door behind them.

Miranda volunteers to lead the diversion team, though Shepard can assign another squad member. An ideal fire-team leader is Garrus, Miranda, or Jacob; a non-ideal choice will result in both the leader and specialist being shot. After this selection, Shepard addresses the troops, giving them a rousing speech before final preparations. Shepard then selects a squad to accompany them into combat, knowing they will face waves of Collectors with repeated Harbinger possessions and time pressure to keep the specialist alive during the vent passage. The team disembarks.
beats.choice: selected tech specialist and fire-team leader

If the base was preserved, the star appears red and he compliments Shepard's decision, grinning contemplatively at a hologram of the intact station.

evidence.text: This is a disambiguation page. It notes that "Suicide Mission" is the name given both formally and informally to the battle that serves as the finale of Mass Effect 2, in which Commander Shepard leads a counterattack against the Collectors, and links to related articles: Omega 4 Relay, Collector Base, Storyline II, the Mass Effect 2 Guide, Stop the Collectors, and the individual mission walkthroughs (The Normandy Attacked, Collector Base: Infiltration, Collector Base: The Long Walk, and Collector Base: Final Battle). Entering the Omega 4 Relay, which no ship had previously returned from, is considered the start of the Suicide Mission.

evidence.text: Commander Shepard's overarching mission during the events of Mass Effect 2 is to defeat the race known as the Collectors responsible for the disappearance of entire human colonies. This culminates in a desperate and daring counterattack into the heart of their territory often referred to within the story as the "suicide mission." - **Omega 4 Relay** \- The Collectors are rumored to operate from somewhere beyond this uncharted mass relay. The Suicide Mission takes its name partly from the fact that no ship to enter the relay previously has ever returned. Entering the relay is considered the start of the Suicide Mission. - **Collector Base** \- Installation thought to be located beyond the Omega 4 Relay from where the Collectors launch their attacks. Primary target of the Suicide Mission. - **Storyline II** \- An in\-universe style narrative encompassing the events surrounding Mass Effect 2 including the Suicide Mission.
evidence.for_key: the Suicide Mission through the Omega-4 relay and the Collector Base assault

evidence.text: After the Normandy crew is abducted by the Collectors, Shepard must decide whether to travel immediately through the Omega 4 Relay to rescue the crew and destroy the Collector Base or to delay the mission in order to prepare themselves better. If Shepard chooses the latter option, the team arrives just in time to see Kelly and other crew members get horrifically dissolved into raw organic material — which Doctor Chakwas describes as paste — used to create the Human\-Reaper. If Shepard chooses to go through the Omega 4 Relay immediately, then Lilith, a colonist from Horizon, is liquefied, but Shepard and the squad free Kelly and the rest of the crew just in time. After releasing them from their pods, Shepard can choose to assign a squad member to lead the survivors back to the Normandy. If Shepard saves Kelly in the suicide mission, the yeoman recalls the events of her imprisonment vividly, reminiscent of Thane's memory recollection.
evidence.for_key: the Suicide Mission through the Omega-4 relay and the Collector Base assault

evidence.text:
The Omega 4 Relay was a mass relay in the Sahrabarik system of the Omega Nebula, surrounded by hazard beacons and automated warnings. Over the previous thousand years many ships had attempted to pass through it and none had returned; the only ships to travel freely back and forth were the mysterious Collectors. Theories about its far end ranged from a black hole to an earthly paradise, but most assumed the Collectors captured or destroyed those who passed.

In Mass Effect 2 it was revealed that the relay led to the galactic core, where the Collector Base sat on the edge of a black hole. Standard relay transit produced a drift of several thousand kilometers, which was fatal in the galactic core, so the area was choked with debris from ships that had used the relay without a Reaper IFF. The Reaper IFF triggered advanced safety protocols in the Omega 4 Relay that ensured a ship survived close approach to the black hole. It was the only known mass relay to glow red rather than blue, and if Shepard survived the suicide mission, Alliance officials were reported to be extremely concerned about the relay's recent use.
evidence.for_key: the Suicide Mission through the Omega-4 relay and the Collector Base assault

evidence.text:
The Collector Base was a massive space station on the accretion disk of a black hole in the galactic core, reachable only through the Omega 4 Relay and, Commander Shepard speculated, shielded by Reaper technology. It was surrounded by the Tartarus Debris Field, a graveyard of ships destroyed attempting the relay, patrolled by hidden Oculi, and kept at least one Collector Cruiser docked. It housed countless Collectors, Seeker Swarms, husks, Abominations, and Scions, along with the Collector General, who was directly controlled by the Reaper Harbinger. After infiltrating and escaping a Collector Cruiser, Shepard pinpointed the base near the Milky Way's core and obtained a Reaper IFF to cross the relay safely. During the suicide mission the Normandy SR-2 survived the Collectors' security systems, destroyed an intercepting cruiser, and crash-landed on the base. Shepard split the squad into teams to fight through Collector troops, husks, and Seeker Swarms, found the kidnapped Normandy crew stored in pods among thousands of humans, and learned the Collectors were breaking victims down into an organic paste piped to another part of the base. At the core Shepard found a Human-Reaper larva built from thousands of abducted humans and seemingly destroyed it by shattering its feeding tubes.

Shepard then opened a terminal to overload the base's reactor, but the Illusive Man asked instead for a radiation pulse that would kill the Collectors while leaving the technology intact for Cerberus to use against the Reapers. Depending on Shepard's response, Garrus, Legion, Zaeed, Grunt, and Mordin argued to preserve the base, while Tali, Kasumi, Thane, Jacob, and Jack objected to keeping it, and Samara and Miranda were neutral. The Human-Reaper climbed back out and was destroyed again before Shepard escaped as the countdown expired, with Harbinger vowing to continue its plans. If Shepard destroyed the base the star behind the Illusive Man appeared pure blue; if the base was preserved, deep red. In Mass Effect 3, Cerberus sent teams through the Omega-4 Relay to salvage Reaper technology from the base whether it had been destroyed or preserved, and incorporated the recovered Human-Reaper into Cronos Station, using it as the station's brain if the base was preserved or its heart if it was destroyed. After the Alliance captured Cronos Station, the Human-Reaper's remains became Crucible War Assets. In an unmodified, unimported Mass Effect 3 game the base had been destroyed by Shepard.
evidence.for_key: the Suicide Mission through the Omega-4 relay and the Collector Base assault

evidence.text:
Stop the Collectors was the main plot mission of Mass Effect 2, acquired automatically after Freedom's Progress once Commander Shepard confirmed the Collectors were behind the abduction of entire human colonies in the Terminus Systems. It consisted of a chain of missions directed by the Illusive Man and ended only when Shepard confronted the Collector Base beyond the Omega 4 Relay.

Shepard first assembled a team using the Illusive Man's dossiers, recruiting a core group (Archangel/Garrus Vakarian, the Convict/Jack, the Professor/Mordin Solus, the Warlord's creation Grunt, plus DLC recruits the Veteran and the Master Thief), and was reunited with Joker and given the Cerberus-built Normandy SR-2, staffed by EDI. After the Collectors attacked Horizon, the Illusive Man provided further dossiers (Tali, the Assassin, the Justicar). Shepard then boarded a disabled Collector ship, where EDI discovered the Collectors used a Reaper IFF to pass the Omega 4 Relay, and the ship proved to be a trap.

To obtain a Reaper IFF, Shepard traveled to a derelict Reaper orbiting the brown dwarf Mnemosyne, fought through Husks with help from a lone geth platform (recruitable as Legion), retrieved the IFF and destroyed the Reaper. While the IFF was being installed and the squad was away in the shuttle, the IFF broadcast the Normandy's position and a Collector cruiser boarded the ship; EDI was unshackled and the player briefly controlled Joker as he purged the Collectors, but the entire crew except Joker was abducted. Shepard then faced a choice: go through the relay immediately to save everyone, or complete more missions and lose half or all of the crew.

Using the Omega 4 Relay, the Normandy emerged in a debris field, fought Oculi and a Collector cruiser (with squad deaths possible if the ship was not upgraded), and crash-landed on the Collector Base. Inside, Shepard learned the Collectors were building a Human-Reaper from abducted humans, faced a final choice to destroy the base or preserve it for Cerberus via a radiation pulse, and had a closing conversation with the Illusive Man mirroring the aftermath of the Battle of the Citadel.
evidence.for_key: the Suicide Mission through the Omega-4 relay and the Collector Base assault

evidence.text: After Shepard dealt with the Collectors, Cerberus sent teams through the Omega\-4 Relay to salvage Reaper technology from the Collector Base, whether it was destroyed or preserved. At Cronos Station, Commander Shepard's team discovers that Cerberus recovered the Human\-Reaper and are using it to augment the station's functionality—either its brain if the Collector Base was preserved or its heart if the Collector Base was destroyed. When the Alliance captures Cronos Station, the Human\-Reaper's remains are incorporated into the Crucible, becoming War Assets.
evidence.for_key: the Suicide Mission through the Omega-4 relay and the Collector Base assault

evidence.text: Commander Shepard's main goal after resurrection is to locate the Collectors' "homeworld" and put a stop to their attacks on human colonies. After infiltrating and escaping a Collector Cruiser, the Collector homeworld is pinpointed near the Milky Way's core. In order to safely cross the Omega 4 Relay, Shepard then locates a Reaper IFF. Once the suicide mission commences, the Normandy SR\-2 arrives at the Tartarus Debris Field. After surviving a sudden attack by the Collectors' security systems, the Normandy destroys the Collector Cruiser sent to intercept it, and crash\-lands on the Collector Base itself. Deciding that the base must be destroyed to end the Collector threat, Shepard divides the squad into several teams to enter the base and overcome its defenses: Collector troops, husks, and seeker swarms. After fighting their way deep into the base, Shepard and company locate the kidnapped Normandy crew, stored alongside thousands of other humans in pods. They discover that the Collectors are breaking down the human victims into an organic "paste," which is being piped off to another part of the base. At the base's core, Shepard finds a Human\-Reaper larva, constructed using thousands of abducted humans. The nascent Reaper is seemingly destroyed when Shepard shatters the feeding tubes that support it, causing it to fall into the depths of the base.
evidence.for_key: the Suicide Mission through the Omega-4 relay and the Collector Base assault

evidence.text:
Collector Base: The Long Walk was the second segment of the Mass Effect 2 suicide mission, triggered after Collector Base: Infiltration. Entering a room holding the colonists and the Normandy crew, Commander Shepard wiped condensation from a pod and found either Lilith from Horizon, if Shepard had gone to the base immediately after the crew's abduction, or Kelly Chambers, if Shepard had done one or more missions first; the occupant stirred, screamed, and was liquefied. Shepard ordered the remaining pods opened, saving the whole crew, half of it, or only Doctor Chakwas depending on how quickly the Commander had departed. Chakwas explained that the Collectors were processing humans into a gray paste of genetic material routed to another part of the station. EDI reported that the only route ahead held too many Seeker Swarms for Mordin's countermeasures, so a biotic had to hold a protective field over a small squad while a second team created a distraction. Shepard chose the biotic specialist, ideally a loyal Samara, Jack, or Morinth; a second fire-team leader, ideally Miranda or a loyal Garrus or Jacob; and optionally a squad member to escort the crew back to the Normandy, since Joker said they had to go backwards. Assigning a non-loyal escort saved the crew but killed that squadmate, while assigning no escort kept all squadmates for the final battle but doomed the crew.

The chosen squad then advanced through the swarm-filled area inside the biotic bubble, where leaving the field meant death, fighting Collectors, Harbinger, husks, Abominations, and a Scion across several stops. During the final run to the security door, if the biotic specialist was non-loyal or non-ideal, the biotic collapsed from exhaustion and whichever squadmate held the rearguard was carried off by the swarm, following a fixed death order; a loyal, ideal specialist pushed the barrier back, sending the swarms and Collectors flying, and everyone reached safety. As the second fire-team leader entered they were shot, shrugging it off if ideal or dying in Shepard's arms if non-ideal, though with only three squad members left any leader survived. Joker then reported on whoever was escorting the crew and warned that the Collectors were massing outside the doors, and Miranda said the rest of the team would stay back to cover Shepard and a small squad. Cut content included unused Mordin voicelines volunteering as the biotic specialist despite his lack of any biotic powers.

evidence.text:
Seeker Swarms were technological devices used by the Collectors, resembling large light-brown insects with four wings, four limbs, and a stinger. Deployed in swarms from Collector ships, they sought out organic targets and stung them, leaving victims in a paralytic, stasis-like state. This allowed the Collectors to disable the population of entire colonies before moving in to gather the bodies for transport.

After the Battle of the Citadel, the Collectors used Seeker Swarms against human colonies in the Terminus Systems. On Freedom's Progress every colonist was taken; the sole survivor was the quarian Veetor'Nara, who had been on his Pilgrimage and, though mentally unbalanced by the attack, recorded footage and biological data of the swarms. He passed this to Commander Shepard, who had begun working with Cerberus against the abductions. After analysis, the Illusive Man asked Shepard to recruit Mordin Solus, who developed an experimental countermeasure making its wearer theoretically invisible to the swarms. It was successfully tested on Horizon during a Collector attack, but proved inadequate against heavy concentrations of Seekers such as those in the Collector Base, where biotic fields were used to hold the swarms back.

In Mass Effect: Paragon Lost, Collectors arrived on Fehl Prime in 2185 and deployed swarms that bypassed the colony's new military-grade kinetic barriers, stunning every human on sight, including James Vega's associates Captain Toni, April, and Christine, and his squadmate Essex, who later recovered thanks to a cure. The swarms were destroyed when their Collector Cruiser was, and Vega later handed intel on the Collectors and the cure to the Alliance.

In 2186, Shepard encountered no Seeker Swarms directly, though "Collector swarms" were reported in the fighting on Palaven. Across galactic battlefields, Collector Captains created swarms that advanced in small dispersible clusters, Possessed Captains created more powerful Seeker Plagues, and some battlefields featured a massive, indestructible swarm that roamed the area harming friend and foe alike. The Awakened Collector Adept could deploy and launch Seeker Swarms as a power.

evidence.text: In the aftermath of the Battle of the Citadel, the Collectors deployed Seeker Swarms on human colonies in the Terminus Systems and began abducting their inhabitants. One such planet was Freedom's Progress, where all human colonists were taken. The sole survivor of the attack was a quarian, Veetor'Nara, who was on his Pilgrimage there. Though mentally unbalanced by the encounter, Veetor had managed to record footage and biological data of the Seeker Swarms. He gives this information to Commander Shepard, who had begun working with Cerberus to stop the colony abductions. After an analysis of the quarian's data, the Illusive Man asks Shepard to find Mordin Solus and solicit his scientific expertise to create a vaccine to repel the paralytic effects of the Seeker Swarms. Mordin later develops an experimental countermeasure that makes wearers theoretically invisible to the Swarms. The countermeasure is successfully tested on Horizon during an ongoing attack by the Collectors. However, it proves to be unable to provide protection against heavy concentrations of Seekers, such as those later encountered by Shepard in the Collector Base, but this is remedied with the use of biotic fields to keep the Swarms at bay. |  | ***“Do you think I made the wrong decision?”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Paragon Lost** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text: - This is a character capable of very potent biotic damage, being able to prime multiple Biotic Explosions with Dark Sphere and Dark Channel and single\-handedly detonate them in quick succession using Seeker Swarms. - A potent biotic attack pattern manipulating the cooldown mechanics is to first send out a Dark Sphere, then Dark Channel (which has a short cooldown), then detonate numerous enemies with Seeker Swarms (make sure you have plenty summoned before initiating the Dark Sphere) and finally, if desired, detonate Dark Sphere. - For this tactic, it is useful to invest points in Seeker Swarm because Dark Channel and Dark Sphere cannot detonate each other. - Dark Sphere can still be detonated manually (triggering the cooldown) even if it has already been used for Biotic Explosions. The detonation may hit enemies through cover. - Alternatively, using Seeker Swarms for the protection bonus and not detonating Dark Sphere allows for a heavier loadout supported by biotic damage\-over\-time. - The Collector suffers from lengthy power cooldowns and activation animations, which can prove untimely in the middle of a battle. Be aware of how many Seeker Swarms you have with you at all times so that the activation animation does not take you by surprise. - If timed correctly, it is possible to cancel the "summoning" animation of the Seeker Swarm by quickly using a Dark Channel. This has the added bonus of activating the significantly shorter cooldown of Dark Channel. - The Collector can gain a whopping \+65% boost to power damage from its passive class power Vengeful Ancient. When equipment and gear are taken into account, the Collector Adept can easily have a more than 100% boost to power damage—and Dark Sphere and Dark Channel both are very high\-damage effects by default. - As an alternative to normal power\-heavy Adepts, with Ascension Mode and the Collector/Prothean Weapon Damage bonuses of Vengeful Ancient, an Awakened Collector specced for weapon damage is one of the best Particle Rifle users in the game. - Ascension Mode's fairly limited 45 second duration coupled with its long activation animation can make it a chore to sustain, so use it wisely. - Forewing Leap functions similar to the Propulsion Packs of the Turian Ghost Infiltrator, Turian Havoc Soldier, and Turian Saboteur Engineer. While it suffers from a significant post\-use delay, its initial movement is extremely quick, making it one of the most reactive dodges in the game.

evidence.text:
The Seeker Plague was a Collector unit encountered in Mass Effect 3, an enhanced variant of the Seeker Swarm. Possessed Collector Captains deployed Seeker Plagues to paralyze opponents, and a Possessed Captain could only have one swarm active at a time.

Once launched, a Seeker Plague pursued players in order to explode near them. Its detonation radius was much larger than that of a normal Seeker Swarm and penetrated terrain. A player caught in the blast took significant damage, had cooldown-based powers disabled for a short period, and suffered greatly reduced weapon accuracy. NPC squadmates were immune to the disabling effects. Powers without cooldowns, such as Nova, Phase Disruptor, and grenade-type powers, were unaffected, as were readied "charge" powers such as Biotic Orbs, Siege Pulse, and the Krogan Warlord Sentinel's hammer powers. The Marksman power, while active, made its user immune to the disabling effect.

Seeker Plagues were individually weak but carried a barrier for added protection. Their small size and erratic, fast movement made them hard to hit, and they could climb short drops and traverse ladders. They could not be frozen or placed in Stasis. Effective counters included area-of-effect and rapid-fire weapons, barrier-damaging powers such as Warp, Concussive Shot, and Overload, and Singularity, which locked down groups of seekers since they never dodged it. Pull could occasionally kill an unprotected seeker instantly. As a swarm prepared to explode it briefly stopped and vibrated more frantically; moving away during that moment could cause it to dissipate, though the larger blast radius made this far harder to escape than with a standard swarm. As a summoned unit, Seeker Plague kills did not count as enemy kills for certain multiplayer purposes, and eliminating all active swarms was not required to complete a wave. Swarms lasted until killed or detonated.

evidence.text:
The Human Vanguard was a cooperative multiplayer class in Mass Effect 3 (distinct from the Project Phoenix Vanguard and the Andromeda class of the same name). Its lore blurb repeated that humans joined the galactic community after discovering a Prothean data cache on Mars in 2148. Vanguards were feared frontline fighters who charged across the battlefield to surprise and destroy enemies in close combat.

The class had 500 barrier and 500 health and used the Alliance Training passive with the powers Biotic Charge, Shockwave, Nova and Fitness. Melee options included a punch sequence, a biotically-charged Biotic Strike heavy melee, and a Biotic Punch grab execution; it could combat-roll to dodge. It was the only class with Nova. Its signature tactic was the Charge-Nova cycle: Biotic Charge restored barriers and granted invulnerability during the animation, allowing a follow-up Nova, repeated continuously. Nova consumed barriers rather than triggering a cooldown; the Half Blast evolution halved its cost and damage for better survivability, and its Power Recharge evolution stacked to a 300% cooldown bonus. Shockwave was the only power usable safely at range to knock down enemies and detonate combos, and the only Vanguard priming power via the Lifting Shockwave evolution. The page details faction tactics: Charge-Nova was near-unstoppable against Cerberus (except Guardians and Atlases), highly effective against Collectors (but Seeker Swarms and Abominations were deadly), risky against Geth (Hunters, Primes and Rocket Troopers could stun), and effective against most Reaper troops, with extreme caution urged around Brutes, Ravagers and especially Banshees, whose glowing/teleport state must never be charged.

evidence.text: |  | Audio: Thermal Clips | | --- | --- | *“Over the last two years, firearms have undergone a major enhancement to manage their waste heat. When the Systems Alliance analyzed detailed battle telemetry, they found that the geth were able to keep up a more sustained rate of fire, giving them a significant advantage over Alliance marines. So the Alliance retrofitted every weapon in service, making a full conversion to the thermal clip system. Thermal clips hold disposable universal heat sinks. Armorers are hurriedly adapting to this increased lethality with new defensive technology like self\-sustaining barrier amps, hardened shield generators, and mass field\-integrated armor. evidence.text:
Biotic amplifiers, usually shortened to biotic amps or bio-amps, were devices that enabled biotic individuals to synchronize the dozens of element zero nodules within their nervous systems so those nodules could form mass effect fields large and strong enough for practical use. Amps could also enhance a specific biotic discipline or talent. Biotics manipulated mass effect fields using these nodules, which reacted to electric stimuli from the brain.

An implant was a surgically embedded interface port into which amps were plugged; such implants were also called "wetware" because of their cybernetic nature. In humans, the implant was usually placed at the base of the skull for convenient access, and the user had to keep it free of contaminants. Implant ports could accept a variety of amps, and there was a growing market for modifications and add-ons. The finest quality implants and amps were manufactured by asari artisans, but the Systems Alliance's L3 implants, first deployed in 2170 CE, marked a significant advance for human biotic amp manufacturers. By 2186 CE, enhanced L3 variants and more advanced L4 and L5 models had been developed, though they remained experimental and not widely used.

In Mass Effect, bio-amp models could be purchased from merchants, obtained in battle, or recovered from storage containers. Amps provided three attributes: a Duration Bonus (increased duration of all biotic talents), a Power Bonus (increased Throw and Lift force, Warp damage, and Barrier strength), and a Cooldown Bonus (reduced recharge times). The Adept, Vanguard, and Sentinel player classes could equip biotic amps, as could the squad members Liara T'Soni, Kaidan Alenko, and Urdnot Wrex. Named models included the Solaris Amp (Aldrin Labs), Prodigy (Armali Council), Gemini (Armax Arsenal), Polaris (Kassa Fabrication), Savant (Serrice Council), and the Unity Amp (Sirta Foundation). The Spectre Gear HMBA Basic, Advanced, and Master lines could only be acquired through console commands.

evidence.text: The **Adept** is the ultimate biotic, able to affect the physical world with the power of the mind. Adepts are durable and powerful manipulators of mass effect fields; they can use biotics to violently manipulate objects in the environment, including nearby enemy targets. Gameplay focus is on disabling and debuffing enemies while dealing massive amounts of damage. Adepts possess all biotic abilities and can wear specialized bio\-amps, but they can only equip light armor and only gain weapons training with pistols. They also possess no tech skills. Biotic powers focus on manipulation of dark energy with Singularity, Lift and Throw. They can weaken foes with Warp and protect themselves with Barrier. The Adept class talent reduces recharge time for biotic talents and increases biotic protection.

evidence.text:
Barrier was a biotic ability appearing in Mass Effect, Mass Effect 2, and Mass Effect 3, distinct from the Andromeda skill of the same name. The page explained that biotic barriers used mass effect fields to protect the user much like a kinetic barrier, but with unique characteristics.

In the first Mass Effect, Barrier was a biotic talent that surrounded the user with a high-gravity mass effect field, effectively strengthening the player's shields for a set period or until the extra points were depleted by damage. It did not protect against physical damage such as melee attacks, explosive ordnance, flying debris, or environmental hazards. It scaled from Barrier (400 points absorbed, 10 seconds) through Advanced Barrier and Master Barrier (1000 points, 23 seconds), and unlocked Stasis at higher ranks. Bastions and Vanguard Shock Troopers gained Barrier Specialization at level 9, which increased strength and duration and let the shield regenerate while taking damage. Classes with access were the Adept, Sentinel, unlockable Vanguard, Asari Scientist, and Krogan Battlemaster. Changing body armor cancelled an active Barrier.

In Mass Effect 2, Barrier created a shield that soaked large amounts of damage, functionally equivalent to Fortification and Geth Shield Boost. It added a percentage of maximum shields (up to +100% with the Heavy Barrier evolution) and could evolve into Heavy Barrier or the longer-lasting Improved Barrier. It uniquely had no activation animation, making Shepard less likely to be interrupted under fire, and could be used while storming. It was available to Shepard via Advanced Training and as Jacob Taylor's loyalty power.

In Mass Effect 3, Barrier reinforced armor with a biotic field that reduced all damage taken while slowing power use, and could be detonated to lift nearby targets in an omnidirectional blast that dealt 1.5x damage to barriers and hit up to three targets. Its rank evolutions included Recharge, Blast Effect, Barrier Strength, Shield Recharge, Power Synergy, and Power Recharge. It was available to Kaidan Alenko, Urdnot Wrex, Jacob Taylor, and Shepard as a bonus power in single-player, and to the Krogan Battlemaster Vanguard and Krogan Shaman Adept in multiplayer. The trivia noted that in Mass Effect: Ascension, Hendel Mitra used a Barrier more like a stationary geth barrier than an in-game biotic Barrier.

evidence.text: Biotic implants and amplifiers only provide the potential to create coherent mass effect fields. Whether biotics can actually do so is largely determined by their training. Biotics must develop conscious control over their nervous systems, sending specific electrical impulses to the element zero nodules embedded in their nerves. They are taught to use their implants and amps with biofeedback devices and physical mnemonics. Specific gestures or muscle movements fire the proper sequence of nerves to activate a certain skill. Conatix Industries pioneered biotic training with the Biotic Acclimation and Temperance Training program. Although BAaT did not achieve the desired results, many techniques taught are still used today. Many human think tanks are trying to develop some form of biotic super soldier. Most are benign efforts to create more flexible troops. Others, less publicly known, are unapologetic attempts to create Nietzschean supermen.

evidence.text: All asari are naturally biotic from birth, though not all choose to develop their abilities. Biotics of other species are individuals who were exposed to dust\-form element zero, or colloquially, "eezo", in utero and subsequently developed eezo nodules throughout their nervous systems. These nodules can generate mass effect fields when energized by electrical impulses from the brain. Eezo exposure is by no means guaranteed to result in biotic ability. On the contrary, most fetuses that are exposed are not affected at all. Others will develop brain tumors or other horrific physical complications. In humans, only about one in ten eezo\-exposed infants will develop biotic talents strong and stable enough to merit training, and these abilities are not always permanent. In extremely rare cases, humans who were exposed in utero but did not manifest biotic talents as children can develop them during young adulthood through additional exposure. Once identified as having biotic ability, a person might be outfitted with a surgically implanted amplifier around the age of puberty. This amplifier is designed to make their talents strong enough to be useful, and some races have experimented with biotic drugs, such as red sand, to stimulate power instead. Once the implant is installed, its user must then develop conscious control over their nervous system, which is a long, slow, difficult ordeal (except for the asari, who naturally possess a degree of voluntary control). Biofeedback therapy is often used to assist the progression of this process, and once they fulfil their training, a biotic can control their emission of dark energy to generate mass effect fields that move objects, generate protective barriers, or restrain enemies. Biotic abilities are activated using a technique called "physical mnemonics", in which the biotic uses a physical gesture to cause neurons to fire in a certain sequence, sending an electrical charge through their eezo nodules and creating the desired effect. A biotic may enhance certain aspects of his or her biotic abilities by installing implant upgrades called bio\-amps. Biotic abilities fall into three general categories: Telekinesis, the use of mass\-lowering fields to lift or hurl objects; Kinetic Fields, mass\-raising fields to immobilize objects (in combat, usually enemy projectiles or enemies themselves); and Spatial Distortion, the creation of shifting mass\-effect fields which rip apart any objects caught within them.

evidence.text:
The Adept was a playable character class in Mass Effect, Mass Effect 2, and Mass Effect 3, and a profile in Mass Effect: Andromeda, focused on biotic power. Described as the ultimate biotic, the Adept manipulated the physical world through mass effect fields, disabling and debuffing enemies while dealing heavy damage.

In the original Mass Effect, Adepts possessed all biotic abilities and could wear specialized bio-amps, but could equip only light armor, gained weapons training only with pistols, and had no tech skills. Their powers included Singularity, Lift, Throw, Warp, Barrier, and Stasis. The Adept class talent reduced biotic recharge time and increased biotic protection, and an Adept could specialize into Bastion or Nemesis to reach levels 7 through 12.

In Mass Effect 2 and Mass Effect 3, Adepts were biotic specialists who lacked advanced combat training but were the best at defeating enemies without firing a shot, outfitted with L5x implants that could spawn a micro-singularity. Mass Effect 2 gave them Warp, Throw, Singularity, Pull, Shockwave, and Biotic Mastery, with weapons training in heavy pistols, submachine guns, and heavy weapons. Mass Effect 3 added Cluster Grenade and Fitness; the Adept had a low weight capacity, comparable to the Engineer, with a bonus rising from 10 to a maximum of 50 through Biotic Mastery.

Mass Effect: Andromeda replaced fixed classes with flexible Profiles that Pathfinder Ryder could swap at any time, including in combat. The Adept profile reconfigured Ryder's implant for biotic combat and offered bonus powers Biotic Echoes, letting biotic combos trigger additional explosions on each enemy touched, and Biotic Jump & Evades, replacing the jump jet with biotic movement. According to franchise statistics, the Adept ranked fourth of six in popularity as a Shepard class, chosen by 7 percent of players in March 2012 and 11 percent by July 2021 in Legendary Edition.

evidence.text: - **Damage Protection** \- This value represents a percentage reduction of the damage that successfully affects a character's health. Usually shields must be depleted first. Any damage inflicted on the character is reduced by the listed percentage. In the case of multiple effects such as Energized Plating (Armor Upgrade) and Immunity (Talents \= Fitness) the percentages are calculated in a series. Example \= (100 damage \- 17% from the armor) \= 83, (83 reduced damage \- 15% Energized Plating) \= 70\.55, (70 reduced damage \- 50% Immunity) \= 35 points of final damage. - **Shields** \- This is the character's first line of defense, and represents the total amount of damage that a character's armor will absorb before affecting their health. - **Tech / Biotic Protection** \- Much like Damage Protection is a percentage reduction of physical damage sustained, Tech / Biotic Protection reduces the amount of time a character is affected by hostile abilities. Additionally, this stat reduces damage from enemy attacks that deal tech or biotic damage specifically, e.g. Warp or the electrical burst attacks of Husks.

evidence.text: Mechanics - Barrier is a biotic power in Mass Effect 2. - Barrier is functionally the same as Fortification and Geth Shield Boost, and differs only slightly from the *Improved* evolution of the latter. - Barrier, being a biotic ability, is eligible for biotic upgrades (e.g. Biotic Cooldown), while Fortification is not. - The bonus from Barrier is added to your total current shields. Barrier therefore expires only when the duration expires or if your shield is ever completely collapsed. - Barrier is unique among the four Mass Effect 2 "armor powers" (the other three being Tech Armor, Fortification, and Geth Shield Boost) in that it does not have an activation animation. - This is actually an advantage, as it means that Shepard is less likely to be interrupted when activating Barrier under fire, e.g. by a pyro's flame stream. It also fits the mental flavor of a biotic ability. - Like Fortification and Geth Shield Boost (but not Tech Armor) Barrier is also one of the few powers in Mass Effect 2 that can be used without interrupting Shepard when storming. - Barrier and the other defensive shield powers can be activated when your shields are down, giving you an immediate recharge. However, be aware that damage to your health does **not** recover from this, and should your shields go down before you are able to regenerate normally, your health will still be compromised. - The graphical effect for Barrier fades much more quickly than Fortification does, and the only way to verify your true current shield maximum is on the Squad tab of the main menu. - Unlocking Jacob's Barrier (on completion of Jacob: The Gift of Greatness) can create the conundrum that he will constantly reactivate it during battles even if Squad Power Use is disabled, making him less likely to use his other powers or be able to use them on demand. The only way to have a loyal Jacob but avoid automatic Barrier activation is to reset his powers using the Advanced Training terminal at the Shadow Broker's Base (requires either Lair of the Shadow Broker DLC or Legendary Edition) and invest no points in Barrier. Strategies - In Mass Effect 2, both Level 4 Barrier evolutions already have a duration far in excess of their cooldown. The Barrier can simply be refreshed if it is about to lapse. Improved Barrier is far less likely to run out at the wrong time during a combat situation if the player is careful not to let their shield break from damage, though Heavy Barrier, being tougher, is easier to keep from being broken by damage. - The long duration of Improved Barrier is helpful for all classes as it enables more use of other powers before it must be recast to renew its duration. This is especially helpful for Soldiers who tend to have the slowest power recharge speeds.

evidence.text:
The N7 Fury Adept was a Mass Effect 3 multiplayer character class representing the "go-anywhere, fight-anything" special forces of the Alliance, trained at the Interplanetary Combatives Academy in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Candidates had to survive combat situations "in an admirable and effective fashion" to earn the N7 rank, and by the time of the Reaper War many N7s were training other species in anti-Reaper asymmetric warfare.

Fury operatives used implants to fuel their biotics and extreme movement speed, weaving an unpredictable path through the battlefield, darting in and out of combat before unleashing sweeping biotic attacks on unsuspecting targets. The class had a 500 barrier and 500 health, and its powers were Throw, Annihilation Field, Dark Channel and Fitness. Its heavy melee, Biotic Strike, teleported the Fury forward and released a biotic burst at the cost of barrier; its grab dragged an enemy over cover for a charged biotic punch; and its dodge, Acrobatics, was a short-range teleport flip that could pass through walls and move between levels. In play, a low-cooldown Fury chained Biotic Explosions by priming enemies with Annihilation Field and detonating with Throw, or with the Dark Channel–Throw combination, moving from enemy to enemy and staggering foes before they could respond.

After years of running these strange jobs, Vetra asked Kesh what they were for only to be shocked by their contributions to the Initiative. Damage to Sid's cryo array caused her to be woken early, during the initial disastrous arrival of the Nexus in Andromeda. Investigations need to start from somewhere, and the M\-11 Suppressor Shepard recovered is chosen as the starting point. **Note:**  Grumbling about your shore leave getting cancelled in this conversation can draw a sympathetic response from your love interest if they are present. Liara then examines the pistol and summons Glyph. Glyph begins compiling data and then Joker walks in with the rest of the crew. At this point you can go around and talk to all crewmembers there. evidence.text:
Mass Effect: Genesis 2 was an interactive backstory comic produced by Dark Horse Comics for Mass Effect 3: Special Edition for Wii U, and released April 2, 2013 for Xbox 360, PC, and PlayStation 3. An updated version of Mass Effect: Genesis, it stood in for both Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2 for new players, summarizing the first two games and letting the player make six choices from each. It was prompted after character creation but was optional, with separate male and female Shepard versions. It could not be used when importing a Mass Effect 2 save into Mass Effect 3.

The six Mass Effect choices matched the original Genesis. The six Mass Effect 2 choices were: how many squadmates Shepard recruited; whether squadmate conflicts were resolved or ignored; whether Shepard stayed true to old friends or moved on; whether Shepard went through the Omega 4 Relay immediately or upgraded the Normandy SR-2 first; whether Shepard started a new romance; and whether the Collector Base was spared or destroyed. The comic omitted Feros, the geth, squadmate recruitment and loyalty missions, other romances, missions such as Horizon, and all DLC content, meaning Kasumi Goto and Zaeed Massani would not appear in Mass Effect 3. Resolving conflicts implicitly resolved all loyalty missions in specific canonical ways (heretics destroyed, Maelon's data destroyed, Morinth killed). Garrus Vakarian always survived the Suicide Mission and always appeared in Mass Effect 3; the "worst" outcome left 8 of 10 squadmates dead. The page includes a table of Suicide Mission survival results by choice combination. It was priced at 320 BioWare Points on PC and $3.99 on Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3, and is included in Mass Effect Legendary Edition.

The fourth part of a hand-corrected video-essay character analysis covered Tali'Zorah in Mass Effect 3. If she survived the Suicide Mission, she apologized to Shepard for the trial and admitted he had been right: "I was too ready to sacrifice myself for the good of the Fleet. I need to stop doing that." She took an Admiral's seat in her father's place specifically to push back against the Board's worst ideas, the version of Tali the essayist preferred. If exiled, she instead told Shepard the trial had shown her she belonged "on the Normandy, helping you," aiding her people from the shadows.

As Admiral she doubted her fitness to command, with seventeen million lives riding on her. After speaking with Legion she believed the quarians could sue for peace, but once Daro'Xen turned Rael'Zorah's research into "an invasion too good to pass up," Tali had no choice but to support it "for the good of the Fleet," regressing toward the sacrificial lamb of ME2 and becoming a near-powerless victim of politics again. The essay noted quarian scarcity: 17 million in the flotilla, one child per family unless the population declines, every quarian contributing to the Fleet's survival. Shala'Raan was the reason Tali was permitted to attempt to retake the Alarei.

At the Rannoch climax Shepard chose between peace, geth genocide, or quarian genocide. Siding with the quarians, Tali killed Legion (or shut the geth down) with a "flat shovel blade," expressed regret, and answered Legion's last question, "Does this unit have a soul?", with "Yes... yes, it does." Siding with the geth, Tali begged Shepard not to choose them over her people, then as Admiral called off the quarian fleet's attack while Legion sacrificed himself to disseminate the code. On the botched path, unable to stop Han'Gerrel, Rael and Daro'Xen, Tali watched what remained of the quarian fleet burn in Rannoch's atmosphere, Captain Ysra of the Rayya on the radio, and took her own life before her home ship burned. Afterward, if the geth helped rebuild Rannoch, Tali admitted: "I'd have killed the geth with no regrets, and I'd have been wrong."

evidence.text:
Kallini: Ardat-Yakshi Monastery was a Mass Effect 3 mission, acquired after Priority: The Citadel II when Liara relayed that Asari High Command wanted Commander Shepard to investigate a distress signal after several asari commando squads vanished. Though titled for the Kallini system, the monastery was actually on Lesuss in the Mesana system of the Nimbus Cluster. On arrival Shepard learned the signal came from an Ardat-Yakshi monastery, which the asari government had been reluctant to disclose. If Samara had survived Mass Effect 2, a recently arrived vehicle indicated her presence, and Shepard met her inside.

Exploring the darkened monastery, the team found asari corpses and logs revealing that Matriarch Gallae and Superintendent Jethra had blocked extranet access to keep students from panicking over Reaper rumors and had refused to evacuate. The mission introduced the Banshee, a Reaper conversion of Ardat-Yakshi, first encountered in the courtyard, followed by Cannibals, Marauders, and Husks. In a cutscene the surviving Ardat-Yakshi Falere begged Shepard and Samara to save her sister Rila from a bomb in the Great Hall, then rushed ahead. Activating the bomb woke Rila, who attacked Falere as indoctrination took hold. After a fight against two Banshees and Husks, Rila took the detonator, insisted her family leave, and declared "The Ardat-Yakshi are not the Reapers' slaves" before setting off the bomb and destroying the monastery. Shepard dragged Falere to the elevator to escape.

In the aftermath, if Samara was present she drew her pistol, saying the Justicar Code required her to kill any Ardat-Yakshi living outside the monastery, and attempted suicide; a Paragon interrupt stopped her, Falere chose to remain, and Samara joined the war effort. evidence.text:
Singularity was a Biotic skill in Mass Effect: Andromeda, the Andromeda incarnation of the trilogy's biotic power of the same name. Tapping the button deployed a gravity well that lifted and damaged unshielded and unarmored enemies and primed enemies for combo detonations; tapping again ended the effect early. At rank 1 it dealt 35 damage per second over a 3-meter radius for 8 seconds, with a 24-second recharge in single-player (20 in multiplayer).

Its rank upgrades improved recharge speed, damage, duration, and radius, added +100% damage versus shields (Anti-Shield), and offered a rank 6 choice between Exploding Singularity, which detonated after the effect ended for area damage in a 7-meter radius, and Expanding Singularity, which grew the radius by 200% over the skill's lifetime. Biotic explosions from primed units did not end the skill. Although a target needed no armor or shields to be lifted, all targets in the area of effect were primed even if protected, though protected enemies could still move out of the field. It functioned mainly as a crowd-control tool against masses of unprotected units and, combined with a detonator, as an effective way to strip shields. It was available to Pathfinder Ryder (unlocked with 9 points in Biotic skills or Biotic Training) and in multiplayer to the Human Adept and Human Commando.

evidence.text:
Commander Vyrnnus was a turian biotic and mercenary who fought in the First Contact War, claiming to have served at the helm of a dreadnought that killed the father of one human trainee. In 2166 the human corporation Conatix Industries hired Vyrnnus and several other turian mercenaries to instruct human teenagers in the Biotic Acclimation and Temperance Training (BAaT) program at the Jump Zero station (also called Gagarin Station). Conatix kept the turians' involvement secret, since public memory of the First Contact War was still raw and human biotics being trained by turians would have angered the Alliance public.

Vyrnnus openly despised humans and ran a severe regime that used hunger and thirst as training aids. Several BAaT trainees "snapped" under the strain and some died. According to Mass Effect: Foundation, one incident began when a boy was caught rigging an illicit off-station transmitter; Vyrnnus tied him to a post, lectured the students on the millions of credits spent on their education, and forced them to biotically assemble objects from a pile of blocks for hours, withholding water. As students collapsed from exhaustion, Kaidan Alenko covered for Rahna when she faltered. Vyrnnus noticed, taunted Rahna with a floating glass of water, then blasted her arm and called her pathetic. In the Mass Effect account he broke Rahna's arm outright.

Kaidan retaliated with a burst of biotic energy. Vyrnnus escalated the confrontation, lunging biotically, drawing a military-issue "talon" knife, goading Kaidan to finish the fight, and slicing Kaidan's right side. Kaidan answered with a biotically charged jumpkick to Vyrnnus's head. The blow was stronger than intended and broke Vyrnnus's neck. BAaT staff tried to give him medical attention, but he died before reaching the infirmary. His death caused a diplomatic incident with the turians and ultimately led to the BAaT program being shut down. By 2183 Vyrnnus was a figure from Kaidan's past that could also be shared with Commander Shepard.

Turians receive the best military training in the galaxy. evidence.text:

Its six ranks progressively raised maximum shields and health, then improved shield and health regeneration and reduced regeneration delay. Rank 4 offered a choice between Resilience (larger bonuses to maximum shields and health, with biotic evades) and Reflexes (bonuses to regeneration rate and delay reduction). Rank 5 offered Barrier Detonation, causing her barrier to explode and damage nearby enemies when her shields dropped, or Barrier Reinforcement, restoring shields to her and allies when she killed an enemy with a power. Rank 6, locked until her loyalty mission Peebee: A Mysterious Remnant Signal was completed, replaced her evade with a biotic teleport and offered either Advanced Reflexes (large damage bonuses at low health) or Advanced Resilience (further maximum health and shield bonuses). Specced for defence, Peebee could become one of the squad's most durable members, second only to Drack in staying power, functioning as a reliable support character despite modest weapon and power damage.

evidence.text:
The Vanguard was a combat class available across Mass Effect, Mass Effect 2, and Mass Effect 3, and as a profile in Mass Effect: Andromeda. Vanguards combined the offensive biotic powers of the Adept with the weapons and armor training of the Soldier, forming the front line of the squad. They used biotics to disable and soften enemies while shielding themselves long enough to finish foes at close range with gunfire. In Mass Effect they wore light armor (upgradable to medium), could gain specialist training in shotguns and pistols, and equipped advanced bio-amps; the class talent increased shotgun and pistol damage and biotic protection, and could specialize into the combat-oriented Shock Trooper or the biotics-oriented Nemesis. All Krogan Battlemasters, including Urdnot Wrex, belonged to this class.

In Mass Effect 2 and Mass Effect 3, Vanguards were known for a high-risk, high-reward style, closing quickly on enemies and destroying them at short range. They were outfitted with L5n implants enabling the Biotic Charge, which struck an opponent with great force while bringing the Vanguard into close combat. Powers included Incendiary Ammo, Cryo Ammo, Charge/Biotic Charge, Shockwave, Nova (ME3), and Pull. In Mass Effect 3 the Vanguard had a weight capacity bonus of 15 to 70 depending on Assault Mastery rank. In Mass Effect: Andromeda the Vanguard profile reconfigured Ryder's implant and physiology to absorb energy from enemies on melee impact and channel it into shields, with bonus powers Siphoning Strikes and Biotic Jump & Evades. By July 2021 the Vanguard was the second most-picked class among Mass Effect Legendary Edition players, used by 21%.

evidence.text:
Charge, also called Biotic Charge, was a biotic power available in Mass Effect 2 and Mass Effect 3, in both single-player and multiplayer. It enveloped the user in a mass effect field that launched them almost instantaneously across the battlefield toward a locked enemy target, ending in a collision that damaged and knocked back most unprotected foes. It required a clear line of sight and a HUD target lock, could not be used to teleport to empty ground, and did not trigger against destructible objects such as explosive canisters. It allowed the user to phase through solid obstacles en route and could multiply physics damage against enemies already levitated by other biotics.

In Mass Effect 2 the power had three ranks before a rank 4 evolution into Heavy Charge, which added force, full shield restoration, and an 80% game-speed slow for 1.15 seconds, or Area Charge, which burst on impact with a 3-meter radius to hit multiple enemies. Recharge time was 6 seconds and range 40 meters at all ranks. From rank 2 onward Charge restored and temporarily boosted the user's shields, the maximum-shield bonus calculated from a base value of 250 and behaving like the Tech Armor bonus. It dealt only token damage, 25/35/45/45 base by rank and 60 for Heavy Charge. It was intentionally unaffected by the Biotic Cooldown upgrade, though Mass Effect Legendary Edition changed this. In Mass Effect 2 it was available to the Vanguard class and to Tela Vasir.

In Mass Effect 3 Charge had six ranks with branching evolutions at ranks 4, 5, and 6: Force & Damage or Radius; Weapon Synergy or Power Synergy; and Bonus Power or Barrier. Base recharge was 10 seconds, 14 for krogan, and the user was invulnerable while the power was in effect. It no longer raised maximum shields; instead a successful Charge granted a 50% damage-reduction buff for 4 seconds and restored 50% of barriers, or 100% with the rank 6 Barrier evolution. Charge dealt 1.5x damage to barriers, completed even if its target died en route, and set up Biotic Explosions when combined with lasting biotics such as Warp or Pull. Alongside Nova it was a Vanguard signature move. It was available in single-player to the Vanguard and in multiplayer to eight Vanguard variants, including the Asari, Krogan Battlemaster, Volus Protector, and N7 Slayer. Trivia noted that the Cabal Vanguard used Poison Strike instead of Charge.

evidence.text:
The Batarian Brawler Vanguard was a playable multiplayer class in Mass Effect 3. The page opened with the standard batarian flavor text, noting that little was known about Khar'shan or its inhabitants and that the race was judged by the organized crime enforcers, pirate boarding parties, slaver gangs, and gladiatorial combatants the Hegemony allowed beyond its borders. Batarians were described as large brawlers who used nets and spiked weapons to capture or bleed targets, and who bludgeoned close opponents with spiked armor and enforcement gauntlets.

The class used the "Batarian Enforcer" archetype with a barrier of 750 and health of 750. Its powers were Biotic Charge, Lash, Blade Armor, and the passive Fitness. Its melee sequence was two one-handed punches and a final two-handed blow; its heavy melee, Enforcement Gauntlets, wound up a powerful omni-tool punch that sent unprotected foot soldiers flying and destroyed their heads on a fatal hit; and its grab dragged an enemy over cover for an Enforcement Punch execution. The Batarian Brawler Vanguard had no dodge maneuver and could take cover but not roll between cover.

Player notes emphasized that the class excelled at melee: starting the heavy melee right after a Biotic Charge let it reach impact with stacked damage reduction, and with powers evolved it could exceed 100% damage reduction by combining heavy melee, Blade Armor, and Biotic Charge bonuses. Because it lacked direct-damage abilities aside from Biotic Charge, the page recommended a light but powerful weapon such as the N7 Piranha for tougher foes like Praetorians and Atlas mechs. Lash could disable smaller foes and set up Biotic Charge detonations on unarmored units but was useless against armored ones, while Blade Armor was best maxed for protection and reflected damage. The notes covered tactics against Cerberus, Collectors, Geth, and Reapers, warning specifically against charging Banshees since batarians could not roll away. A bug caused the Batarian Brawler Vanguard and Batarian Slasher Adept to use male human vocalizations when grabbed by a Husk or Abomination.

evidence.text:
The Project Phoenix Vanguard was a playable multiplayer class in Mass Effect 3, one of the Project Phoenix operatives. Project Phoenix was a result of the Illusive Man's early experiments in enhanced human physiology, producing highly skilled combat and biotic specialists. After the Illusive Man adopted indoctrination to ensure his troops' loyalty, many Phoenix operatives defected to the Alliance to fight the Reapers. Their command of Cerberus lash and stasis technology, backed by strong biotic skills, made them valuable on the battlefield.

The Vanguard had 500 barrier and 500 health and used Biotic Charge, Lash, Smash and Fitness under Phoenix Training. Its regular melee was a shock baton, its heavy melee swung biotically charged lashes, and its grab dragged an enemy over cover for a charged biotic punch. Lash worked like a damaging, long-range Pull that could be evolved for shield and barrier penetration. The class could single-handedly create biotic explosions on armored enemies by pairing Smash with Biotic Charge, with Charge also restoring barriers for survivability. Smash produced a short-range, cover-piercing shockwave effect and, with its Biotic Combo evolution, left a priming effect on any target including large armored units, uniquely letting this Vanguard benefit from Warp Rounds' biotic damage bonus against hard targets like Atlases.

evidence.text: - As the name might imply, the Batarian Brawler Vanguard excels in melee combat as a skill build. In particular, his long build\-up but unmatched melee synergizes flawlessly with Biotic Charge: by starting the heavy melee right after the charge sequence begins, he can be at the point of impact with a stacked damage reduction right out of a charge, essentially meaning he can 'brawl' enemies with a one\-two of the Charge\-Heavy. - With his powers properly evolved, the Batarian Brawler can easily achieve over 100% damage reduction, combining the stacked bonuses from heavy melee, Blade Armor and Biotic Charge. - With the right timing, when following up a heavy melee on a unprotected target (just health) that has been launched far after a Charge, the Brawler will literally slide along the ground until reaching the target and successfully hitting him with the punch. - The Batarian Vanguard lacks virtually any direct damage in his abilities except for Biotic Charge, and is therefore not suited to go toe\-to\-toe with bigger, tougher foes like Praetorians or Atlas Mechs. Take a powerful but light weapon, such as the N7 Piranha and equip it with a Shotgun High Caliber Barrel. This will allow you to deal with more powerful foes. - Lash will stop most of the smaller foes from being able to fight you, but will prove worthless against armored units. - Lash can, however, set up detonations for Biotic Charge against unarmored units. - Blade Armor should ideally be maxed out, specced for protection and reflect damage. This will make the Brawler much more difficult to kill. - A moderately light loadout is highly recommended, to keep Biotic Charge cooldowns fairly low while maintaining weapon dominance between charges. Or, if you want to spec yourself for melee damage, take a light shotgun (such as the N7 Piranha) or a close\-combat heavy pistol (such as the M\-358 Talon) with melee mods in order to maximize lethality in hand\-to\-hand combat.

evidence.text: - The Phoenix Vanguard's Lash ability functions similarly to Pull, except that targets are dealt considerable damage and thrown a good distance. With the Shield Penetration evolution, Lash can be set up to penetrate shields and barriers. Lash can also be used as a primer for Biotic Explosions, with the Fast Recharge evolution increasing the short time that Lash's biotic effect affects a target. - The Phoenix Vanguard is capable of single\-handedly creating Biotic Explosions on armored enemies by using Smash and following it up with Biotic Charge (or vice\-versa). This enables the Phoenix Vanguard to take down armored units even quicker and enhance survivability by restoring barriers with Charge. - Smash creates a short\-ranged Shockwave\-esque effect that can travel through cover. This is useful against basic infantry enemies, since Smash's high damage will likely kill them; it also enhances longevity as Smash otherwise exposes the user for a long time if cast in the open. - The Biotic Combo evolution of Smash leaves a biotic combo priming effect on any target, including large armored targets. This makes the Phoenix Vanguard the only Vanguard class that can benefit from the biotic damage bonus of Warp Rounds on hard targets like Atlases on its own, giving the class a potentially large edge in weapon damage alongside hard\-hitting powers.

evidence.text: - Compared to the Human Vanguard, this character is slower, but with greater survivability and a much stronger melee attack. Almost every Charge should be followed with a headbutt, and Rage combined with Fortify will quickly make him deal punishing damage to any reachable target, all while being nearly impervious to light weapons fire. - As with other characters with Charge, this character can be suited for Retrieval and Devices waves provided there's an enemy to Charge to nearby. An active Fortify will slow the vanguard down a bit, but worth it if under heavy fire. - Thanks to Rage Rank 2, the Krogan Vanguard can bring a decent combination of rapid\-fire pistol and a hard\-hitting pistol or shotgun without going overweight. If there are enough skills left for APEX Training, the extra 10% equates to about 85 units total weight capacity, which should be sufficient for carrying the heaviest weapons with few issues. - The Krogan Vanguard's primer skills are locked behind rank 6 evolutions and are only useful in close range, effectively meaning no long\-distance detonation setups before Charging in. To pull off combo detonations with Charge without relying on outside factors, investing in ammo boosters is recommended. - A Krogan Vanguard can approach an enemy (through walking/dashing) to trigger the Fortify purge first then Charging point\-blank to trigger a tech detonation. Multiple clumps of enemies can be demolished nearly instantly through this method. The process is more efficient if Shock Trooper is selected for Charge rank 6 and recharge times are optimized for fast cooldowns, allowing for Charge spamming and triggering detonations every second Charge. - Purge \+ Charge can also be used as a quick escape from flanking units if one or more manage to sneak up on blind sides. - Nova is of limited use to the Krogan Vanguard due to the focus on melee damage. There are other abilities worth allocating skill points to while the character hasn't reached Rank XX yet. - As with all Vanguard characters, care must be taken to avoid getting killed by enemy units with grab/insta\-kill melee attacks. - Put Sharpshooters, Anointed, and Observers on second priority if within line of sight. Oftentimes the "killing blow from nowhere" can be traced to them while the Krogan Vanguard is busy dealing with enemies at closer ranges.

evidence.text: - The Human Vanguard is the only character to have the Nova power, allowing for a unique play style that shouldn't be underestimated. - The Human Vanguard can be a deadly ally on the battlefield, as Nova can stun, stagger and destroy enemies time after time. As Biotic Charge recharges barriers, this allows the player to always follow up with a single Nova (or two with the Half Blast evolution) and then rinse and repeat. With that in mind, Vanguards are heavy\-hitting biotic combat specialists that can completely control the battlefield and live up to their names (Vanguard is a military term for those who are 'First\-in'). - Because a Human Vanguard's strength is in their biotics, a light loadout is recommended. - Nova shares some of the mechanics of grenade powers: it doesn't trigger a cooldown, but is limited in use: it can be used as long the Vanguard has barriers. - With a Volus Adept or Vanguard (with Biotic Orbs evolved for maximum recharge speed) standing next to you and constantly using Shield Boost, Human Vanguards will never have their barriers depleted, allowing for successive Nova usage. - On higher difficulties, it may be wise to take the Rank 5 Half Blast evolution of Nova. This will reduce the damage of Nova by 40%, but will also reduce its barrier consumption by half. This will increase your overall survivability, since you will still have some barriers left for emergencies (for example, being staggered by large opponents like Brutes and Geth Primes after executing a Nova attack). If some enemies are left alive from the first blast, you can always use your remaining barriers to unleash a second Nova attack. - Nova's Power Recharge evolution bonus stacks up to 4 times, effectively giving the Vanguard a **300% cooldown bonus**. This allows for a higher\-damage Charge/Nova cycle with a smaller window of vulnerability than Charge/Nova/Nova, since the Vanguard is invincible while using either power. Using power efficiency Equipment and Gear can shorten the vulnerability window but not eliminate it. - While one may choose to neglect Shockwave in favor of Charge and Nova, Shockwave is the only power that can be safely used from a distance (up to 24 meters) to knock enemies off their feet and detonate Power Combos, with potential bonus damage when detonating Biotic Explosions. Shockwave is also the Human Vanguard's only means of priming enemies for biotic combos through use of the Lifting Shockwave evolution. Detonating enemies lifted by the power generally must be done with Nova, as enemies are not suspended long enough for Charge to come off cooldown. Also, as enemies tend to fly up out of reach of Nova when hit by Lifting Shockwave, this works best where vertical space is confined (i.e. there is a ceiling).
